title: Amazing, Beauteous Change
description: Amazing, Beauteous Change in Tonic Solfa to DARWALL, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 312 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Wilderness Transformed. Is. 41:18, 19”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.4.4.4.4), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DARWALL; any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-ma-zing, beau-teous change! A world cre-a-ted new! My thoughts with trans-port range, The love-ly scene to view: In all I trace, The work is thine; Sa-viour di-vine, Be thine the praise!

lines: No more they rend the slain.
And thirst for blood no more;

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to DARWALL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
